U1: Revisit design for _ID_ and _TimeStamp_ attributes in Tuple, refactor to improve performance throughput.
U2: Document Kryo optimization guidelines.
U3: Upgrade to Kafka 0.8.2.
U4: Create a Tuple load-generator to measure Tuple-based payload performance.
U5: Create a new load-generator for highly optimized (kryo serialized) payload.
U6: Rerun baseline, Tuple, and Serialized payloads to compare performance between Kafka 0.8.1 and 0.8.2.

technical_and_design_decisions: Reuse the existing Spring XD performance test harness and module framework as the foundation for both new load-generators, rather than building a new benchmarking framework from scratch.

Implement the Tuple load-generator (U4) as a standalone Java/Spring XD source-module style application that emits Tuple payloads at configurable rates, so it directly reflects production XD message paths.

Implement the optimized load-generator (U5) using Kryo serialization via the existing XD codec/serializer infrastructure, ensuring the serialized payload path matches what production tuning would use.
For the Kafka 0.8.2 upgrade (U3), migrate to the new Kafka 0.8.2 producer API while keeping consumer-side compatibility, and update dependency management (Gradle build) accordingly.

For the Tuple refactor (U1), replace mandatory _ID_ and _TimeStamp_ attributes with lazily computed or optional fields guarded by configuration, after confirming no downstream component depends on them unconditionally; keep backward compatibility for persisted/serialized tuples.

Run comparative benchmarks (U6) on the same dedicated cluster hardware for both Kafka 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 to guarantee comparability of results, reusing the baseline numbers methodology from the 1.1.1 benchmarking.
Deliver U8 as a design spike only: a written design document with options analysis for native stateful stream processing in XD; no production implementation in this increment.
Publish benchmark documentation (U2 and U7) in the project's existing documentation/blog channels (markdown/asciidoc in-repo plus the project blog).
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; one workday equals 8 hours of focused effort.
The existing Spring XD codebase (with the 1.1.1 baseline benchmark data against Kafka 0.8.1) is available and builds cleanly at the start of the increment.
Benchmark hardware/cluster and cloud resources are already provisioned and available; infrastructure procurement and provisioning effort is excluded.
Kafka 0.8.2 upgrade requires adapting to API changes in the producer and minor configuration changes, but no broker-side migration tooling is needed for the test environment.
The Kryo library is already integrated in the codebase (used for existing serialization), so U5 builds on it without new dependency evaluation.
Documentation targets existing publishing platforms (project wiki/blog), so no new publishing tooling setup is required.
U8 covers requirements study and design only; implementation of stateful stream processing is out of scope for this increment.
Estimates include unit testing, self-review, and integration verification performed by the developer, but exclude elapsed waiting time for external code reviews or CI queue delays.

activities.activity_name: Analyze Tuple design and ID/TimeStamp necessity (U1)
activities.activity_description: Review the Tuple class design, trace usages of the _ID_ and _TimeStamp_ attributes across the codebase, and determine whether they can be removed, made optional, or computed on demand to improve throughput. Produce a short findings note guiding the refactor.

Implement the Tuple refactoring according to the A1 findings: remove or make optional the _ID_ and _TimeStamp_ attributes, adjust constructors, serializers/codecs, and all affected call sites and downstream components.

activities.activity_name: Update and run tests for Tuple refactor (U1)
activities.activity_description: Update existing unit and integration tests impacted by the Tuple changes, add tests covering the new optional/lazy attribute behavior, run the full test suite, and verify no regressions.

Author end-user facing documentation describing Kryo serialization tuning and optimization guidelines (registration, buffer sizing, serializer choices) with examples, aimed at improving payload performance.
Update build dependencies to Kafka 0.8.2, adapt the integration code to API changes (notably the new producer API), adjust configuration properties, and resolve compilation and runtime issues.

Run integration and smoke tests of stream processing over Kafka 0.8.2 (produce/consume paths, failure/restart scenarios) and fix any defects found to confirm the upgrade is functionally sound before benchmarking.
Design and implement a configurable load-generator producing Tuple-based payloads (rate, size, and tuple shape configurable) suitable for measuring Tuple payload performance through the XD pipeline.
Test the Tuple load-generator for correctness and stability: verify emitted payload structure, sustained target rates, and accurate measurement/logging of throughput and latency.

Design and implement a second load-generator that emits highly optimized Kryo-serialized payloads, using the existing XD Kryo codec/serializer infrastructure, with configuration parity to the Tuple generator for fair comparison.
Verify the serialized load-generator produces valid Kryo payloads decodable downstream, sustains target rates, and records comparable metrics to the Tuple generator.

Set up and configure two equivalent benchmark environments, one with Kafka 0.8.1 and one with Kafka 0.8.2, including XD deployment, topic configuration, monitoring, and metrics collection for repeatable runs.

activities.activity_name: Execute benchmark runs on both Kafka versions (U6)
activities.activity_description: Run baseline, Tuple, and Kryo-serialized payload benchmarks against both Kafka 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 (multiple runs per scenario for stability), collecting throughput, latency, and resource utilization data.
Consolidate, clean, and analyze the collected benchmark data; compute comparative statistics between 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 and between payload types; prepare charts and key findings.

Document the performance benchmark results together with infrastructure specifics (hardware, cluster sizes, versions, configuration) and publish as a reference blog/guide for users setting up a Spring XD cluster.
Research and document the requirements for stateful stream processing in XD: state scoping, persistence/fault tolerance, checkpointing, and interaction with the existing stream deployment model.

Brainstorm candidate designs for native stateful stream processing in XD, evaluate trade-offs, and produce a design document with a recommended approach, architecture outline, and open questions for a future implementation increment.
